title: Elegant
paragraphs: “A national character so hopelessly rotten? I’m starting to feel like giving up on them.”
“That’s not very graceful, is it? Sometimes it’s necessary to admit defeat and offer up a part of yourself to ask for forgiveness, don’t you think?”
Yuki-chan is cutting through the prevailing sentiment in Shieldfreeden quite decisively, isn’t she? That she can be quite harsh at times is a sign of her sharp intelligence.
“I’d like to think the commoners aren’t quite that bad…”
“It looks like we’ll have to ask the people about this. Fortunately, Shieldfreeden seems to be somewhat democratic, at least on the surface.”

By the way, it’s only natural to feel very uneasy about that “somewhat democratic” part. After all, despite everything, there’s a history where the races that served as representatives at the time of the nation’s founding by immigrants have continued to govern as representatives to this day. I suppose there’s a possibility for civilians to become lawmakers as well, isn’t there? Though Father and Finacées from my original world muttered that they were just figureheads.

In other words, while they preach freedom, power shifts based on race, not ability. After all, almost all of the successive Aotatsu leaders have held power. In that sense, power was even more concentrated among a select few races here than it was in Siltvelt.

“Well… this is another world, and I get that you’re supposed to ‘when in Rome, do as the Romans do,’ but… with the threat of the Waves looming, we shouldn’t be able to afford to say things like that.”

That’s true. If this were a crisis facing the world—or a world without the ‘Waves’—I’d probably have just thought, “Do whatever you want.” The old me would have thought, “There’s no point in me, a foreigner from another world, getting involved.” However, for the sake of the truly peaceful world I promised to Filo, I must change what needs to be changed.
“Can’t we get support by using the ‘Shield Hero’ name?”
“You should be revered as a god among the Demi-Humans.”
“For someone in that position, you seemed pretty laid-back, though. I figured that was Takt’s fault, though…”
“As for Shieldfreeden… well, I’m not entirely sure myself, but I remember religious matters being a hassle. In particular, I think there were some Blue Dragon tribes that saw themselves as saints.”
“So, does that mean they didn’t worship the Shield Hero?”
“He’s technically on the divine throne, though. But doesn’t that just mean there are plenty of others besides him? I’m not an expert, so I don’t know any more than that.”

Hmm… that’s quite a hassle, isn’t it? Well, I wasn’t really involved in that much in the first world or during the previous loop, so I don’t know much about it. Back in the game days… I only knew of countries similar to Faubrey. I was too busy hanging out with those pigs to delve deeply into the world’s lore. I only know the basics of its overall history.
“I guess I’ll need to ask around and do some research at the next meeting… Lasa, could you look into it for me when you have some free time outside of guarding me?”
“Sure thing. It might be a good opportunity to have a little chat. I’ll look into it later.”
With that, Father stopped hugging and petting the panda from behind and started playing around with Sakura-chan. Maybe that finally relieved her mental fatigue, because she gave me her usual smile.
“Well… what should we do next?”
“Isn’t it time for a bath?”
“You’re right. Motoyasu-kun… still peeping, as usual?”
“If I can peek, I’ll do it.”
“I always wonder this, but what does the Spear Hero actually want?”
“They say that when a girl is seen while being peeked at, her charm goes up. Even Eclair-san was dumbfounded by that.”
“If that’s all it takes to boost their charm, wouldn’t life be a breeze?”
“I suppose so…”
“As for the rest, well… since we already have a portal, we could return to Siltvelt, couldn’t we?”
We could even go to Melromarc, if we wanted. If you rest in Siltvelt—which is practically as safe as your own home—you won’t have to worry about any unnecessary attacks or the like.
“Yeah. I know that, but Siltvelt… well, it’s just not a place where I can really relax. Who knows what might happen if I don’t have Lasa or Sakura keeping an eye on me…”
“I suppose that’s why you’re always eager to go out and explore places like Faubrey and such.”
“Well, since we’re at it, why don’t we head to Zeltoble? If we pretend to be wandering adventurers, we can easily find a place to stay.”
Father seems to waver a bit at my suggestion.
“It’s a very tempting proposal, but I need to stay here to draw the enemy’s attention… so let’s wait a few days.”
“So you really do want to go, don’t you? I think it’s a good idea—I’d like to go to Zeltoble for fun, too.”
“Well then, since we’ve had a bit of a change of pace, let’s go take a bath.”
“Got it!”
With that, we wrapped up our conversation and headed for the baths.

And so, we ended up taking a bath. By the way, the baths that Shieldfreeden had prepared weren’t the usual kind where the women’s section is separated by partitions; instead, they were in a rather uninteresting layout, located in a room a short distance away. It was mainly a shower area, and the bath itself wasn’t exactly “sloppy”… but rather, it had a structure like a fountain. Through the glass window at the back, you could see the moon.
After washing myself, I stepped into the bath, tossed my hair back, and struck a pose with the large window as my backdrop.
Whoosh!
My hair dances gracefully.
“Whoa! That looks fun! Kou wants to do it too!”
“Go ahead. Kou, follow my lead.”
Just like me, Kou finished washing up, stepped into the bath, and tossed his hair back.
Splash!
His hair dances gracefully.
“You guys are playing some weird game that’s kind of annoying… It’s fine here since we’re washing up, but don’t do that where other people are—it’ll bother them.”

Father is scolding us with the same air of someone who’s reluctantly allowed a child to dive underwater at a hot spring because there were no other guests around. Eventually, Father slowly finishes his shower and steps into the tub. However… this tub is a bit small—or rather, it really does just look like a fountain.
“Well then, let’s do it together, Father. First, place your hand on your forehead and wipe the droplets off your hair…”
“No, I’m not doing that.”

I thought my kind Father might go along with it, but he doesn’t seem interested at all. Personally, I thought Yuki-chan would like it, so I wanted to practice making the movements more refined and elegant, but oh well.
“Well then…”

The women’s section here is a little ways away, but it’s possible to peek in. It feels like I might be able to see if I crawl out the window and make my way along the Wall. Specifically, each bath is set up in a protruding, bumpy section of the Wall. In other words, if I climb out the window and move along the Wall, I should be able to see the women’s bath window.

I open the window and look around. Security searchlights are illuminating the area here and there. And security guards are constantly patrolling the area. What’s more, it feels like there are lookouts in the sky as well… Security is tight.
“Motoyasu-kun? What are you doing?”
“Of course I’m going to peek. No matter how difficult it may be, I simply must see not only Yuki-chan but Sakura-chan as well.”
I raise my spear and prepare my Cloaking Lance and Fire Mirage.
“Seriously, if you’re going to sneak in, why not just go through the changing room?”
“Father, that won’t do. It’s precisely because we’re undertaking a difficult mission that it’s meaningful.”
“No, I can’t get behind that logic.”
“The moon is so pretty!”
“That’s true. Kou, you shouldn’t imitate Motoyasu, okay?”
“Huh?”
Hmm… There’s something about Kou’s attitude—I get the feeling he’s secretly looking down on Father. I watch Kou while doing my warm-up exercises.
“Kou.”
“What?”
“You shouldn’t underestimate Father. Otherwise… you’ll end up in a very scary situation.”
“Hmm?”

I have to find a way to make Kou understand. If this were the original “World Standard” version of Father—or if his older sister were here—Kou would calm down, but that’s unlikely in this world. Father is already very kind, and as for his older sister… given the timeline, she’s probably already dead. Is there any good way to reason with Kou without angering my current Father?
That’s what I thought… but since neither Keel nor Mole are here, maybe it’ll be okay. What I need to watch out for is when those kinds of creatures show up.
I mean, small animals… It’s not like there aren’t any Siltvelts or Shieldfreedens around. I’ll have to be careful about that.
But! Right now, we’re just peeking.
“Are you coming too, Father?”
“No, I’m not. And you shouldn’t go either, Kou.”
“Is it fun to see people naked? Kou doesn’t really get it.”
Hahaha, it might still be a bit too early for Kou. The time will come when he understands. After all, in the first world, Kou is already married.
“Well, in Filolial form, it’s practically like being completely naked, so it’s only natural he doesn’t get it.”
“Well then, Father, it’d be a big help if you could cast an Air Strike Shield. We can use it as a foothold.”
“No way! Why do I have to help you guys?!”
“Please, just this once! But I’d really appreciate it if you could spare us the Air-One-Way Shield.”
If we use that as a foothold, we’ll just slide right off.
“No, I’m not doing it.”
“If I don’t take a peek soon, Yuki-chan and the others are going to get overheated. Alright, here I go!”

Whoosh! I went into stealth mode, slipped through the window, and moved swiftly along the Wall like a ninja, using every tiny foothold and handhold I could find to make my way toward the women’s bathhouse.
“I wonder where all that enthusiasm comes from…”
Father muttered as he watched me move swiftly past the window. Don’t you get it? I’m going because that’s where the Land of Eternal Bliss is.

And just like that, I somehow managed to reach the roof above the women’s baths. There was one spot along the way where I had no choice but to jab the wall a little with my spear to keep from falling, but overall, things went smoothly.

Well then… Now I’ll cling to the wall from the roof and peek through the window while hanging upside down. My hair’s sticking to me, which is a bit annoying. But I’ll put up with it. After all, this is the Land of Eternal Bliss.

Then I see Yuki-chan gracefully stretching out her legs as she soaks in the tub, striking a pose. She’s well aware that I’m watching her. I suppose this means Yuki-chan is growing up into a woman. As Father, Motoyasu, I couldn’t be happier.
“...What on earth are you doing?”

Panda and Sakura-chan are staring blankly at Yuki-chan like that, looking utterly dumbfounded. By the way, when Sakura-chan gets in the bath, she reverts to her Filolial form. At first glance, Yuki-chan is the only one who’s naked.
“I’m studying elegant and refined poses, assuming that Lord Motoyasu is watching me.”
“Oh, I see…”
“Hmm… Sakura, I want to take a bath with Naofumi.”
“You’re a kid—why don’t you just ask him?”
“Eclair told me I couldn’t.”
“If he’s the Shield Hero, I think he’d let you in if you asked…”
“Really? Then I’ll go ask Naofumi!”

And just like that, Sakura-chan transformed from her Filolial form back into an angel. What a shame. Wait a minute… Sakura-chan is actually Filo-tan. Which means if I go back to the men’s bath right now, wouldn’t my dream of bathing with Filo-tan come true?
Whoaaaaaa! …But, Filo-tan is Filo-tan! Sakura-chan is Sakura-chan, after all!
No, think this through. Filo-tan… no, Sakura-chan bathing with Father… what if, by some mistake, Father were to make a move on his own daughter!? I’d be in a real pickle.
“Motoyasu-sama! Are you watching Yuki!?”
Yuki-chan is scanning the area, seizing this moment. She’s worried I might not be watching her. I’ve been hiding, but maybe I should show myself to put her mind at ease?
…I guess I have no choice. I’ll cancel my stealth mode and keep peeking through the window so Yuki-chan and the others can spot me.
“Seriously, you’re such a weirdo… If your charm went up just from being watched, life would be so easy—Eek!?”

The panda looked my way and, for some reason, let out a scream. She noticed me pretty quickly. Just as you’d expect from a top-notch mercenary. But what was that scream about? Oh, was it because I was spotted?
“W-wait, there’s a face above the window!?”
The panda pointed at me, trembling and shouting at the top of her lungs. You’re making too much of a fuss! We’ll get caught!
“It’s Lord Motoyasu!”
“Huh!? The Spear Hero!? I totally thought it was some kind of evil spirit. Is it because your hair’s wet and standing on end?”

For a mercenary, do you actually believe in evil spirits? Well, given examples like the Ghost Crimson Swine, I can’t exactly rule it out. I suppose a mercenary’s job is to be hated by enemies, but I guess even they’re scared of what scares them.
“I’m right here!”
“How did you… You really understand the struggles of the Shield Hero, don’t you? Just get back to the men’s bath already!”

As she said that, the panda began chanting a Magic spell. What on earth is she planning to do!? Casting a disruption spell would be one option, but I’m a man with some sense of decorum. After all, if I get caught, getting scolded is part of the deal.
“Zweite Bend Bamboo!”

A bamboo stalk slithered out from the panda’s hand, snaking along the Wall to appear right next to me, and then—thwack!—it slammed me down. I could have stayed put if I’d braced myself, but this is a punishment, after all.
“Whoa!”
Speaking flatly, I used the bamboo’s flex to launch myself toward the men’s bath area as if I’d been blown away by the Wind.
“Ah, Motoyasu-sama!”
“Well then, Yuki-chan, farewell!”

Waving to Yuki-chan, I grabbed the ledge leading to the men’s bath area and made my way back inside. By the way, it seems Sakura-chan had been given a quick shower by Father before being kicked out of the bath. It was quite an elegant bath time, wasn’t it?
